facts.statement: Liaoningotitan is a medium-sized sauropod estimated to reach a body length of 10 meters and a shoulder height of 2 meters.
facts.quote: Liaoningotitan is a medium-sized sauropod, with an estimated body length of 10 m and shoulder height of 2 m based on comparisons with the closely related Euhelopus.

facts.statement: Liaoningotitan is distinguished by a convex ventral margin of the maxilla and a short, anteriorly positioned upper tooth row.
facts.quote: Distinguishing features of Liaoningotitan include a ventral margin of the maxilla that is convex, an upper tooth row that is short and anteriorly positioned

facts.statement: Liaoningotitan possesses nine reduced, un-imbricated lower teeth with asymmetric, elliptical-like crowns featuring lingual grooves, ridges, and a bulbous basal crown.
facts.quote: nine reduced and un-imbricated lower teeth; asymmetric lower tooth crowns which are elliptical-like in cross section, with lingual grooves and ridges and a lingually bulbous basal crown

facts.statement: A redescription of the holotype specimen proposed that Liaoningotitan is affiliated with the family Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: A redescription of the holotype proposed affinities of Liaoningotitan with the Euhelopodidae.

facts.statement: Zhou et al. (2018) classified Liaoningotitan as a somphospondylan titanosauriform that is more derived than Euhelopus.
facts.quote: Zhou et al. (2018) recovered Liaoningotitan as a somphospondylan titanosauriform more derived than Euhelopus.

facts.statement: In a 2025 redescription, Bingqing Shan proposed that Liaoningotitan belongs to the Euhelopodidae family as the sister taxon to Yongjinglong.
facts.quote: In a 2025 redescription of the holotype specimen, Bingqing Shan proposed that Liaoningotitan was a member of the Euhelopodidae, as the sister taxon to Yongjinglong.

facts.statement: Liaoningotitan lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
